instruction: Looks reasonable. Go ahead, while also brainstorm and investigate if there's other more elegant and general solution for this (e.g., some neural/probablistic approach?).
scope: Practical neural/probabilistic claim-to-logic parsing, without retraining SRL or multimodal models.
sub_questions: Can grammar/AST constraints replace ad hoc repairs?
Can a small neural model choose faithful logical forms?
How can uncertainty over meanings enter probabilistic logic?
Do pretrained AMR/DRS parsers remove the conversion bottleneck?

papers.title: PICARD: Parsing Incrementally for Constrained Auto-Regressive Decoding from Language Models
papers.authors: Torsten Scholak; Nathan Schucher; Dzmitry Bahdanau
papers.method: Reject inadmissible next tokens through incremental parsing.
papers.results: Improves Spider/CoSQL performance in the paper.
papers.relevance: Validity constraints are useful infrastructure; they do not certify source meaning.
papers.verification: Primary venue, author implementation or arXiv page opened; no numeric result inferred where not supplied.

papers.title: Synchromesh: Reliable code generation from pre-trained language models
papers.authors: Gabriel Poesia; Oleksandr Polozov; Vu Le; Ashish Tiwari; Gustavo Soares; Christopher Meek; Sumit Gulwani
papers.problem: Generated programs violate language or contextual constraints.
papers.method: Constrain partial completions with syntax, scope and type checks; retrieve similar program examples.
papers.results: Reports complementary improvements from constraints and retrieval on three program languages.
papers.relevance: A general completion checker is more systematic than adding isolated output-string rules.
papers.verification: Primary venue, author implementation or arXiv page opened; no numeric result inferred where not supplied.

papers.title: Grammar-Constrained Decoding Makes Large Language Models Better Logical Parsers
papers.authors: Federico Raspanti; Tanir Ozcelebi; Mike Holenderski
papers.method: Apply output grammar constraints to LLM logical parsing.
papers.results: Reports improved syntactic correctness and semantic accuracy on its tasks.
papers.relevance: Relevant comparison; a grammar does not supply a faithful reference interpretation for our claims.
papers.verification: Primary venue, author implementation or arXiv page opened; no numeric result inferred where not supplied.

papers.title: CRANE: Reasoning with constrained LLM generation
papers.authors: Debangshu Banerjee; Tarun Suresh; Shubham Ugare; Sasa Misailovic; Gagandeep Singh
papers.problem: Restricting every token to a final-answer grammar can inhibit reasoning.
papers.method: Augment the grammar to permit reasoning while constraining the final structured answer.
papers.results: Provides a theoretical analysis and task evaluations.
papers.relevance: A concise semantic analysis before JSON is worth comparing; this is not a faithfulness guarantee.
papers.verification: Primary venue, author implementation or arXiv page opened; no numeric result inferred where not supplied.

papers.title: Grammar-Aligned Decoding
papers.authors: Kanghee Park; Jiayu Wang; Taylor Berg-Kirkpatrick; Nadia Polikarpova; Loris D'Antoni
papers.problem: Token-local constraints distort the sampled sequence distribution.
papers.method: Approximate grammar-conditioned generation with adaptive sampling.
papers.results: Shows improved likelihoods on structured generation tasks.
papers.relevance: Decoder scores are not automatically a calibrated posterior over meanings.
papers.verification: Primary venue, author implementation or arXiv page opened; no numeric result inferred where not supplied.

papers.title: Semantic Parsing to Probabilistic Programs for Situated Question Answering
papers.authors: Jayant Krishnamurthy; Oyvind Tafjord; Aniruddha Kembhavi
papers.problem: Question interpretation and environment interpretation are uncertain.
papers.method: Parse questions into probabilistic programs and infer over language/environment choices.
papers.results: Evaluates situated question answering with approximate structured inference.
papers.relevance: Direct prior work for uncertain parsing plus uncertain perception. This combination alone is not a novel contribution.
papers.verification: Primary venue, author implementation or arXiv page opened; no numeric result inferred where not supplied.

papers.title: Weakly-Supervised Neural Semantic Parsing with a Generative Ranker
papers.problem: Weak denotation supervision permits spurious logical forms.
papers.method: Rank generated tree-structured programs using execution and utterance agreement.
papers.results: Reports competitive results on three Freebase datasets.
papers.relevance: A source-conditioned neural ranker is plausible; a correct verdict alone cannot identify the correct parse.
papers.verification: Primary venue, author implementation or arXiv page opened; no numeric result inferred where not supplied.

papers.title: Enforcing Consistency in Weakly Supervised Semantic Parsing
papers.authors: Nitish Gupta; Sameer Singh; Matt Gardner
papers.problem: Programs can produce the right answer for the wrong reason.
papers.method: Enforce consistent phrase-to-program mappings across related inputs.
papers.results: Reports a ten-point absolute improvement over its prior best NLVR comparison.
papers.relevance: Controlled role/scope contrasts can constrain parsing without using media truth to choose a convenient reading.
papers.verification: Primary venue, author implementation or arXiv page opened; no numeric result inferred where not supplied.

papers.title: One SPRING to Rule Them Both: Symmetric AMR Semantic Parsing and Generation without a Complex Pipeline
papers.authors: Michele Bevilacqua; Rexhina Blloshmi; Roberto Navigli
papers.problem: Complex separate pipelines for AMR parsing and generation.
papers.method: Use one pretrained encoder-decoder architecture with graph linearization for both directions.
papers.results: Provides models and implementation for AMR parsing/generation.
papers.relevance: A reusable neural frontend; AMR-to-logic still requires correct scope and source alignment.
papers.verification: Primary venue, author implementation or arXiv page opened; no numeric result inferred where not supplied.

papers.title: Neural Semantic Parsing with Extremely Rich Symbolic Meaning Representations
papers.authors: Xiao Zhang; Gosse Bouma; Johan Bos
papers.problem: Lexical copying and frequent-sense defaults weaken symbolic predicates.
papers.method: Train neural DRS parsers with taxonomical concept representations.
papers.results: Improves out-of-vocabulary concept handling; not superior on all standard metrics.
papers.relevance: DRS is an alternative logic-oriented frontend. The linked repository documents training/results; a ready inference checkpoint was not confirmed.
papers.verification: Primary venue, author implementation or arXiv page opened; no numeric result inferred where not supplied.

papers.title: Modeling Quantification and Scope in Abstract Meaning Representations
papers.authors: James Pustejovsky; Ken Lai; Nianwen Xue
papers.problem: Basic AMR has gaps in quantification and scope.
papers.method: Extend the predicative graph with scope structure.
papers.results: A representation proposal rather than evidence for our corpus.
papers.relevance: Replacing SRL with AMR alone does not remove scope design or conversion work.
papers.verification: Primary venue, author implementation or arXiv page opened; no numeric result inferred where not supplied.

papers.title: ChopChop: A Programmable Framework for Semantically Constraining the Output of Language Models
papers.authors: Shaan Nagy; Timothy Zhou; Nadia Polikarpova; Loris D'Antoni
papers.problem: String-level constraints make program semantics difficult to enforce.
papers.method: Prune possible abstract syntax trees using explicit semantic properties.
papers.results: Demonstrates type safety and program-equivalence constraints.
papers.relevance: Elegant general framework for checkable AST properties. It does not turn an uncertain sentence interpretation into a formal equivalence oracle.
papers.verification: Primary venue, author implementation or arXiv page opened; no numeric result inferred where not supplied.

papers.title: Divide and Translate: Compositional First-Order Logic Translation and Verification for Complex Logical Reasoning
papers.authors: Hyun Ryu, Gyeongman Kim, Hyemin S. Lee, Eunho Yang
papers.problem: Complex logical meaning is hard to translate in one generation.
papers.method: Parse component/dependency structures, translate progressively, and compare alternative formulas using a solver.
papers.relevance: Clause-by-clause translation is a stronger next experiment than expanding one monolithic prompt. Solver agreement is not proof of faithfulness to a media claim.

papers.title: Few-Shot Natural Language to First-Order Logic Translation via Code Generation
papers.problem: How to generate complex logical forms without task-specific fine-tuning.
papers.method: Use in-context learning and progressive code generation as an intermediate representation.
papers.results: Reports improvements over training-free translation baselines.
papers.relevance: Supports testing a short structured construction interface; never execute arbitrary model-generated Python in our compiler.

papers.title: A Continuation Semantics for Abstract Meaning Representation
papers.authors: Kenneth Lai; Lucia Donatelli; James Pustejovsky
papers.problem: AMR scope and projection require explicit logical semantics.
papers.method: Translate AMR to first-order logic with continuation semantics.
papers.results: Provides a compositional interpretation for scope phenomena.
papers.relevance: A principled AMR-to-logic converter is an alternative to matching SRL noun heads. Its semantics still depend on faithful input graphs.

papers.title: Squib: Expressive Power of Abstract Meaning Representations
papers.problem: AMR needs a formal logical interpretation and expressive-power analysis.
papers.method: Give recursive translations to first-order logic and analyze negation/quantification.
papers.results: Identifies limitations and extensions for scope.
papers.relevance: The graph-to-logic stage can follow established formal semantics, while neural parse correctness remains a separate empirical question.

papers.title: NL2LOGIC: AST-Guided Translation of Natural Language into First-Order Logic with Large Language Models
papers.authors: Rizky Ramadhana Putra, Raihan Sultan Pasha Basuki, Yutong Cheng, Peng Gao
papers.problem: Fragile syntax and low semantic faithfulness in text-to-logic translation.
papers.method: Recursively parse clauses into an abstract syntax tree; deterministically generate solver code.
papers.results: Evaluates syntax, semantics and downstream reasoning separately on FOLIO, LogicNLI and ProofWriter.
papers.relevance: Very close precedent for separating semantic parsing from deterministic compilation. That separation alone cannot be our novelty; the future paper must establish the multimodal binding/evidence contribution.
papers.verification: Author PDF timed out; independently verified through current ACL venue page and arXiv metadata on2026-11-13.

themes: Typed decoding prevents malformed structure, not mistranslation.
Probabilistic parsing and neural reranking are established.
An unparsed or unfaithful claim is not equivalent to insufficient evidence for a known claim.
Use strict typed structure with defeasible language annotations; inspect meaning separately.

gaps.statement: Formal validity and faithful claim meaning need separate supervision and evaluation.
gaps.evidence: p1-p3,p7,p12; our 61 complete/9 retained development result.

gaps.statement: Language uncertainty must remain distinct from evidence uncertainty and unrepresented meaning.
gaps.evidence: p5-p8; probabilistic parsing and spurious programs are established.

gaps.statement: A broad neural frontend still needs source spans, scope and an implementable conversion to the existing logic.
gaps.evidence: p9-p11; local AMR experiments already exist.

gaps.statement: Parser annotations can be wrong; hard agreement with one annotation is not semantic gold.
gaps.evidence: Our Robot sweep-kick example; p10 discusses predicate/sense weaknesses.

gaps.statement: Limited checked program labels favor small diagnostic comparisons before new parser training.
gaps.evidence: Only 63 unique reviewed final programs in the latest pool; p7-p8 require more structured learning signals.
